Learn the market by reading it closely

Leoside Equity publishes one written research report a day on companies listed in New York and London and on the Indian market. It is written for readers who want to follow the reasoning behind a view, and it is free to read with an account.

What it is

Leoside Equity is a written research publication. It publishes one report a day, each on a single subject: a listed company on weekdays, and the Indian market or one of its sectors at the weekend.

Each company report works through its subject the way an analyst would. It starts with how the business makes its money and how much of that money turns into cash, asks what protects those earnings from competitors, compares the share price with the author's own estimate of value, and closes with what could change the picture. The order is the same every time, and it is set out in full on the research method page.

Nothing here tells you what to buy or sell. A report shows how a view was reached, with its figures and assumptions stated, so that you can test the reasoning, disagree with it and form a view of your own.

Who it is written for

The reports are written for readers who want to understand a business before forming an opinion about its shares. That includes people learning how to read company accounts, private investors who prefer an argument to a tip, and professionals who want a second, independent reading of a company they already know.

No background in finance is assumed. Terms are explained where they first appear, and the method page ends with a glossary of the measures the reports use most. After a few reports, annual reports and results announcements become considerably easier to read unaided.

What a report contains

Every report follows the same layout, so that any two can be compared.

Headline and summary
The argument in one line, then the case for it in two or three sentences. Both are visible to everyone, signed in or not.
Key figures
For a company listed in New York or London: the valuation stance, the fair value band, the price when the report was written, and the horizon the view is framed around. The method page defines each one, and the research disclaimer explains what they do not mean.
The report itself
Divided into sections with their own headings, which are listed beside the text so you can move between them. The reading time and the word count are given under the headline.
Disclosures
At the end of every report: who published it, when it was filed and first published, and a reminder that it is general commentary.
Corrections
If a report is found to contain a factual error, a dated note at the top says what was wrong and what changed. Nothing is edited out quietly.

The week

Each day has a fixed market, which means the subject of the next report is always known in advance, and two reports on the same market can be read one after the other.

MarketDays
United StatesMonday to Wednesday

Independence

Leoside Equity does not accept payment, shares or any other benefit from a company in return for coverage or for a particular conclusion, and no report is sponsored. The site carries no advertising and does not sell or rent anything it holds about its readers.

Reports are published under the Leoside Equity name. The people who write them may own shares in the companies they write about, and reports do not say whether they do, so read each one as the view of someone who may have an interest in its subject and judge the argument on its merits.

Leoside Equity is not registered with any securities regulator, so its reports do not carry the protections that regulated research carries. The research disclaimer explains what that means for you.

Reading and your account

Anyone can browse and search the archive, and read each report's headline, summary, key figures and first 90 words. A free account opens every report in full. There is no card to enter and no paid tier.

An account also keeps a list of the reports you save and a record of those you have read, and lets you choose which markets to follow. Everything held about you can be downloaded as a file, or deleted together with the account, from your dashboard at any time. The privacy policy sets out what is held and where.

Common questions

Is this investment advice?

No. Everything published here is general commentary written for education. It does not take your finances, goals, tax position or appetite for risk into account, and it is not an offer or a recommendation to buy or sell anything. Read the research disclaimer before relying on any report.

Is Leoside Equity registered with a regulator?

No. Leoside Equity is not registered with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, the US Securities and Exchange Commission, FINRA, the UK Financial Conduct Authority or any other regulator, and holds no licence to give investment advice.

Do the authors hold positions in what they write about?

They may. Reports are published under the Leoside Equity name and do not say whether the author owns shares in the company discussed, so read each report as the view of someone who may have an interest in its subject.

Why do the Indian reports not rate individual companies?

Research on securities listed in India is regulated by SEBI, and Leoside Equity is not registered with it. The Indian weekend reports cover the market as a whole or a sector, with no stance, price target or horizon on any individual Indian listed security.

Does it cost anything?

No. Reading is free with an account and there is no paid tier. If that ever changes, account holders will be told in advance and nobody will be charged without agreeing to it first.

Can I share or republish a report?

Share the link freely, and quote a short passage with credit and a link. Republishing a whole report, or using the reports to train or build a commercial product, needs written permission. The terms of service have the detail.

How do I delete my account or get a copy of my data?

From the Account and privacy section of your dashboard. Download my data gives you everything held about you as a file. Delete my account erases the account and everything attached to it straight away.

Something in a report is wrong. What happens?

Write to support@leosideequity.com with the word Correction in the subject. Corrections are added to the top of the report with the date and a note of what changed.

Are reports updated when the share price moves?

No. A report records a view on the day it was published, and the prices in it are those at the time of writing. Factual errors are corrected at the top of the report, but a report is not rewritten because the market has moved. Always check the date before treating a view as current.

Why is most of each report kept for account holders?

The full text is free, but it is kept behind a sign in so that it reaches readers who have confirmed their age and accepted the terms. Signed out, you can still read the headline, the summary, the key figures and the first 90 words of every report.

Can I suggest a company for a report?

Yes. Write to support@leosideequity.com with the company's name and where it is listed. Every suggestion is read. There is no promise that a company will be covered, and a suggestion has no bearing on what a report concludes.

Contact

Questions, corrections, disagreements and company suggestions all go to support@leosideequity.com. Every message is read.
